newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall sharply on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall sharply on political uncertainty.

text.p: Delhi shares closed sharply lower in thin trade on Monday as speculators and foreign investors increased selling on political uncertainty, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 9.74 points down at 876.20.
Brokers said the market was swept by a wave of nervous selling, sparked by confusion in the government over the fate of three ministers who belong to the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) party.

"It seems that bear operators who were forced to stay on the sidelines for a long spell managed to regain control of the market in the short term to some extent, thanks to political instability," said Ashok Arya of brokers S.C. Gupta.
The RJD was founded earlier this month by Laloo Prasad Yadav, a powerful political leader whom the Central Bureau of Investigation has indicted in a $280 million embezzlement scandal.

Yadav, who says he is innocent, resigned on Friday as chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar and installed his wife, Rabri Devi, as his successor. She won a confidence vote in the state assembly on Monday.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition decided on Friday not to admit the RJD in its fold, but left the question on the continuation of its three federal ministers to Gujral.
State Bank of India dipped 5.95 rupees to 317.75.
